title: The Americas and Africa

pages.message: A roving window of 10 days was used to visualize the seasonal patterns of lightning.

note: Ours: the flashes within 70° of where the globe looks on the equator, weighed by how long the station watches each latitude, split between the hemispheres; each hemisphere's daily amount as a 7-day mean, a share of the side's busiest hemisphere-day, square-rooted; the noon sun's latitude; a weighed sample of the flashes.

sources.source: Quality Controlled Lightning Imaging Sensor (LIS) on International Space Station (ISS) Science Data, through the ISS LIS browser of NASA MSFC
sources.license: NASA data, no restrictions on use
sources.credit: Blakeslee, R. J., et al. Lightning Imaging Sensor (LIS) on the International Space Station (ISS). NASA GHRC DAAC / NASA MSFC.
sources.substitute: EIC cites V1 of the same dataset; its link no longer answers, and V3.0 on GHRC needs an Earthdata login. The browser prints the same quality-controlled flashes publicly, one table per orbit.

units.level: share of the track's busiest hemisphere-day, square-rooted (0 to 1)
